hints: Resolve forces parallel to the hill (down the slope) separately for the trailer ($750\text{ kg}$) and the van ($4500\text{ kg}$).
For the trailer moving downhill, the forces acting down the slope are its component of weight $mg \sin \theta$ and the tow-bar tension $T = 450\text{ N}$, opposed by resistance $300\text{ N}$.
Apply $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ to the trailer to solve for $a$, then apply $F_{\text{net}} = Ma$ to the van (or whole system) to find the driving force $D$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law down the hill to the trailer ($750\text{ kg}$), where weight component is $750 \times 10 \times 0.05 = 375\text{ N}$, tension is $T = 450\text{ N}$, and resistance is $300\text{ N}$:
$$375 + 450 - 300 = 750a \implies 525 = 750a \implies a = \frac{525}{750} = 0.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law down the hill to the van ($4500\text{ kg}$), where weight component is $4500 \times 10 \times 0.05 = 2250\text{ N}$, tow-bar tension pulls back with $450\text{ N}$, and resistance is $2500\text{ N}$:
$$D + 2250 - 450 - 2500 = 4500a$$
$$D - 700 = 4500(0.7) = 3150 \implies D = 3150 + 700 = 3850\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Set up the equation of motion down the slope for the trailer. The forces acting down the slope are the component of the trailer's weight $m_t g \sin \theta$ and the forward pull of the tow-bar tension $T = 450\text{ N}$. Opposing the motion up the slope is the resistance force $R_t = 300\text{ N}$:
$$m_t g \sin \theta + T - R_t = m_t a$$

Divide both sides by $750$ to determine the acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{525}{750} = \frac{7}{10} = 0.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Now set up the equation of motion down the slope for the van ($M_v = 4500\text{ kg}$). The forward forces down the incline are the driving force $D$ and the component of the van's weight $M_v g \sin \theta$. The opposing forces up the incline are the backward tension of the tow-bar $T = 450\text{ N}$ and the resistance $R_v = 2500\text{ N}$:
$$D + M_v g \sin \theta - T - R_v = M_v a$$

Add $700$ to both sides to find the driving force $D$:
$$D = 3150 + 700 = 3850\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Applying Newton's Second Law: Forms $525 = 750a$ to obtain $a = 0.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $D - 700 = 4500a$ to obtain $D = 3850\text{ N}$.
